questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 16 cm and a height of 3 cm. What is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 16 × 3 = 24 cm². Halving matters — don't just multiply base by height.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: If reactants react completely inside a sealed container, how does the mass of the products compare to the reactants?
questions.why: In a closed system no matter escapes, so the mass of products equals the mass of reactants.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What is it called when a solid suddenly forms as two liquids react together?
questions.why: A precipitate is a solid that forms unexpectedly when two solutions react, showing a new substance has been made.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: On a nutrition label, what does the energy value mainly tell you?
questions.answer: How much fuel the food provides
questions.why: The energy value (in kJ or calories) shows how much fuel the food gives the body — it says nothing about freshness, shelf life, or how natural the ingredients are.
options: How much fuel the food provides
How fresh the food currently is
How quickly the food will spoil
